comment_encoding.description: Each comment references an exact submitted-text template in its reason_group. Replace {{location}} with file + ':' + baseline_line; the resulting UTF-8 text has the per-issue SHA-256. Candidate suggested comments are never substituted for actual receipt comments.
comment_encoding.checksum: SHA-256 of the reconstructed UTF-8 submitted comment, without a trailing newline added by this ledger

mcp_success_criteria: Included entries have an explicit success:true MCP payload with the matching issueKey and newStatus:falsepositive, and no isError:true. Per-key current issue-status verification is recorded separately.

ascii_locale_identifier.reason: Release-language identifiers deliberately use an ASCII-only character class; Python Unicode \w changes accepted inputs.

comment_templates.c_a41e1317ada4197d: False positive: the suggested replacement changes the validation contract. metadata() deliberately validates language codes with re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*', code), permitting ASCII identifiers only. Python's Unicode str regex \w additionally accepts letters/digits such as é, 中文 and full-width １２, so replacing the suffix character class would accept ené, en中文 and en１２. tests/test_localization.py explicitly verifies these are rejected while en, zh_CN and en_001 are accepted. The explicit ASCII class preserves the release-language path/identifier contract.

gcc13_print_portability.reason: The supported Linux toolchain selects GCC 13; libstdc++ first provides P2093R14/std::print in GCC 14.1.

comment_templates.c_83e9e7703907bdfd:
Portability false positive at {{location}} (main analysis revision 66cbd148). The shared/Linux source is built with the supported GCC 13 baseline selected by .github/actions/dependencies/action.yml (gcc-13/g++-13 and CC/CXX). GCC's official libstdc++ status table records P2093R14/std::print as first available in GCC 14.1, so the recommended <print> API is absent from the supported standard library. Retain the existing printf-family diagnostic.
References: https://github.com/1298345095/wxnotepad/blob/ac6528a5be81b9e3288139efe4a0a9bd087ec317/.github/actions/dependencies/action.yml ; https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/status.html
comment_templates.c_837f2db217d4ef82:
Portability false positive at {{location}}. The supported Linux CI toolchain explicitly installs and selects GCC 13 in .github/actions/dependencies/action.yml. GCC's official libstdc++ implementation status records P2093R14/std::print as first available in GCC 14.1. Replacing this shared diagnostic with std::print would require <print>, which the supported Linux standard library does not provide. Preserve this fprintf call for the supported compiler baseline.
References: https://github.com/1298345095/wxnotepad/blob/ac6528a5be81b9e3288139efe4a0a9bd087ec317/.github/actions/dependencies/action.yml ; https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/status.html

literal_string_termination.reason: The strlen arguments are immutable NUL-terminated literals from local fixtures or the syntax registry.

comment_templates.c_627aa6e44a7b8da3: Reviewed source-to-sink at main 66cbd148 / cleanup ac6528a5. ToggleBlockComments is called by EditorFrame's block-comment command with the SyntaxCommentsFor result. Every enabled close delimiter is a static NUL-terminated literal from the constexpr syntax registry or SyntaxCommentsFor's embedded-language choices (e.g. "*/", "-->", "--", or "]]"). The caller requires rules.open, and all enabled open/close pairs have non-null close literals. Document text controls the selected lexer/style, not the delimiter bytes or storage. std::strlen(close) therefore scans a valid terminated literal; no unterminated input reaches this call.
comment_templates.c_bc4ff9e791659f69: Reviewed source-to-sink at main 66cbd148 / cleanup ac6528a5. EditorFrame calls ToggleBlockComments only when rules.open is non-null. SyntaxCommentsFor obtains open from constexpr syntax definitions or returns fixed embedded-language delimiters such as "/*" and "<!--". These are NUL-terminated string literals with static storage; no document bytes or external pointer become the delimiter. std::strlen(open) cannot over-read an unterminated buffer on this call path. Preserve the original delimiter-search and Undo behavior.
comment_templates.c_cbd22a8d11bf06ca: Reviewed at main 66cbd148 / cleanup ac6528a5. Commands() constructs its Fixture initializer list locally; fixture.token is always one of the NUL-terminated string literals "value", "const", or "color". std::strlen only receives those literal pointers and cannot read an unterminated external buffer. The test then selects exactly that fixed token before checking embedded-region block comments. False positive: the reported buffer over-read precondition is absent.

scintilla_byte_character.reason: GetCharAt transports an unsigned-char result through the pointer-sized message interface; every result fits int.

source_locations: src/editor/word_completion.cpp: Collector::Call and Sci_Position document positions

comment_templates.c_66fe74c6f746f785: False positive for {{location}}. Reviewed the pinned Notepad4 core 89b8b36e0ee2c23f73be922315f17261ccfbbe1a and Collector::Call/EditorControl::Send. Editor.cxx:6997-6998 returns Document::UCharAt; Document.h:618 declares unsigned char, so the full result is 0..255 and fits int. This statement consumes a character/style result, while document positions in this path remain Sci_Position. The pointer-sized transport type does not imply a wider value range for this message.

scintilla_character_value.reason: GetCharacterAndWidth transports an int result through the pointer-sized message interface, preserving its original value range.

comment_templates.c_518ba68ab945bcd9: False positive for {{location}}. Reviewed the pinned Notepad4 core 89b8b36e0ee2c23f73be922315f17261ccfbbe1a and Collector::Call/EditorControl::Send. Editor.cxx:7000-7001 returns Document::GetCharacterAndWidth; Document.cxx:1105-1137 defines its result as int. The intptr_t message transport widens that int and the caller converts it back without losing information; the separate byte-width output uses Sci_Position. This statement consumes a character/style result, while document positions in this path remain Sci_Position. The pointer-sized transport type does not imply a wider value range for this message.

wxwidgets_window_ownership.reason: wxWidgets owns top-level windows and deletes them through Destroy/pending deletion and application cleanup.

comment_templates.c_08fe21e1d6e318d4: Reviewed wxWidgets v3.3.3 ownership. MeasurementApp::OnInit creates a top-level wxFrame, registers its test callback, and calls frame->Destroy() after both successful checks and caught test exceptions, followed by ExitMainLoop(). wxTopLevelWindowBase::Destroy queues the window in wxPendingDelete; wxAppConsoleBase::DeletePendingObjects deletes queued objects and wxAppBase::CleanUp/DeleteAllTLWs releases remaining top-level windows. The frame is framework-owned and follows its deferred native destruction contract. Adding an independent smart-pointer owner would introduce competing deletion. Source: wxWidgets v3.3.3 src/common/toplvcmn.cpp, src/common/appbase.cpp, src/common/appcmn.cpp.
comment_templates.c_55c2fbf5e30ce9dc: Reviewed wxWidgets v3.3.3 ownership. WrapResizeApp::OnInit creates an EditorFrame (wxFrame), presents it, and its AfterPresentation callback calls frame->Destroy() and ExitMainLoop() after either successful checks or caught test exceptions. The SettingsStore remains owned by the wxApp until cleanup. wxTopLevelWindowBase::Destroy uses wxPendingDelete; wxAppConsoleBase::DeletePendingObjects and wxAppBase::DeleteAllTLWs perform framework deletion, including remaining top-level windows on cleanup. This allocation has a native framework owner; independent unique_ptr/shared_ptr ownership would conflict with deferred destruction. Source: pinned wxWidgets v3.3.3 common top-level window and application cleanup implementations.
